notes.title: Russian + Italian
notes.content:
Chroma Zero is now playable in Russian and Italian!

That's probably the last localization coming online for a while, though if anyone is interested in helping with a LATAM Spanish version I think that would still be great to include. Otherwise that makes 13 total languages available! Thank you so much to everyone involved in the localizations. :)

As always if you have feedback on any localizations, good or bad (ideally constructive...) come visit the discord and let me know.

Other fixes are also in this build:
FOV change adjusts on-screen even when you're paused
One particular Zero is available post-credits if you hadn't found it before then

notes.title: 20250804 Patch Notes - small geometry & lighting updates
notes.content:
Nothing crazy, it's just tiny stuff that makes me like the game that much more :)

Zero fades out a little more cleanly

The Temple geometry overlaps less in places

(those things make a certain effect look more clean)

Lighting/shadows for some objects was popping in/out at some angles & distances, I think that's all better now

Have fun!

notes.title: Ongoing Localization Beta
notes.content:
Hi! Chroma Zero now has a beta build live on Steam, which I update regularly to test new localizations. I'm happy to invite everyone to participate. The beta build password is YouAreAwesome. Please let me know about any problems by joining the discord. 

Currently the beta supports:

Simplified Chinese
Polish
Japanese
Brazilian Portuguese
Korean
German
Dutch
Spanish (Spain)
Ukrainian

They will move into the public build on May 27th.

notes.title: Localizations for Chroma Zero
notes.content:
Hello! I'm happy to write that some very generous players have been localizing Chroma Zero into a number of languages. It's a fan/community effort so I don't want to promise any timelines, but things are going well and I expect to release a number of localizations by the end of May. 

In the coming weeks I'll post more about our progress. For now, here's the update:

From the code side of things, Unreal Engine has a really nice set of localization tools that power everything, and I've already adapted the game to work with it. Other aspects like the Menus, in-world text, color vision deficiency text, etc. are also working well. 

On the translation front, currently translations in Simplified Chinese and Polish are done, so we'll start testing there. A number of other languages are making great progress as well, but I will mention them as they're completed. 

If anyone would like to help test, translate, or give feedback, please jump in the discord!
